questions.text: The Hajj pilgrims are required to wear Ihram at a location known as?
questions.explanation: The designated boundary where Hajj pilgrims must enter the state of Ihram is called Miqat. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hajj (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Ziarat-e-Tawaf is considered to be what in Islamic rituals?
questions.explanation: Ziarat-e-Tawaf is considered Faraz (obligatory) in Islamic rituals. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hajj (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: From which Miqat do pilgrims from Pakistan wear ihram?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims from Pakistan (and the Indian subcontinent) wear ihram at Yalamlam, the Miqat designated for those coming from the direction of Yemen and the south. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hajj.

questions.text: Which pillar of Islam demonstrates the principles of brotherhood, equality, punctuality, and discipline?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the pillar of Islam that demonstrates the principles of brotherhood, equality, punctuality, and discipline through its collective rituals performed at specified times. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hajj.

questions.text: On which date do pilgrims perform Rami-Jamrat at all three jamarats?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims perform Rami-Jamrat at all three jamarats on 11th Zil Hajj. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, hajj.

questions.text: What is the first pillar of Islam?
questions.explanation: The first pillar of Islam is Shahadatain (the declaration of faith: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His Messenger"). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: Which Kalma is considered the primary declaration of faith for Muslims?
questions.explanation: The primary declaration of faith for Muslims is Kalma-e-Tayyaba. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: What is the serial number of the Kalimah 'Radd-e-Kufr' among the six Kalimahs?
questions.explanation: The Kalimah 'Radd-e-Kufr' is the Sixth Kalimah among the six Kalimahs. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the Arabic word 'shahadah'?
questions.explanation: The Arabic word 'shahadah' means testimony, and it refers to the declaration of faith in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: How many essential beliefs are articulated in the Iman-e-Mufassal for a Muslim's faith?
questions.explanation: Iman-e-Mufassal articulates 7 essential beliefs of a Muslim's faith. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: What is the second fundamental belief in Islam after the belief in the oneness of Allah?

options.C: Belief in the Day of Judgment

questions.explanation: The second fundamental belief in Islam after the belief in the oneness of Allah is Belief in Angels (Mala'ika). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: How many Kalimas are there in Islam?
questions.explanation: There are six Kalimas in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: Belief in pre-destination is which article of faith in Islam?
questions.explanation: Belief in pre-destination (Taqdeer) is the sixth article of faith in Islam. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, kalma faith.

questions.text: Salat-e-Kasoof is offered during which astronomical event?
questions.explanation: Salat-e-Kasoof is offered during a solar eclipse. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, salat (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is the term for the declaration made before starting the Namaz (prayer)?
questions.explanation: The declaration made before starting the Namaz (prayer) is called Takbeer-e-Tahreema. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, salat.

questions.text: Which Islamic prayer is performed after midnight and before dawn?
questions.explanation: The prayer performed after midnight and before dawn is Tahajud, a highly recommended voluntary (nafl) prayer. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, salat.

questions.text: What did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) declare as the key to Paradise?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) declared Salat as the key to Paradise. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, salat.

questions.text: How far must a Muslim travel to perform Qasr prayer according to Islamic jurisprudence?
questions.explanation: Note: the Hanafi Qasr distance is 48 miles (about 77–78 km). According to the majority of Islamic jurists, a Muslim must travel a distance of approximately 78 km (48 miles) to be eligible for Qasr prayer. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, salat.

questions.text: In which Hijri year was fasting (Roza) made obligatory for Muslims?
questions.explanation: Fasting (Roza) was made obligatory for Muslims in 2 A.H. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum (marked as a past-paper MCQ).

questions.text: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Saum' in Islamic terminology?
questions.explanation: The literal meaning of the word 'Saum' in Islamic terminology is Refraining/Abstaining. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: Which pillar of Islam is metaphorically referred to as 'armour' for its protective benefits?
questions.explanation: Saum (fasting) is metaphorically referred to as 'armour' because it protects a believer from sins and evil desires. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: What is the meaning of Eid-ul-Fitr in Islam?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr means Breaking fast, celebrated at the end of Ramadan. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: What is the practice of Etikaf in Islam?
questions.explanation: Etikaf is the practice of seclusion in the mosque during the last ten days of Ramadan for worship and devotion. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: According to the Hadith, what is considered the Zakat of the body?
questions.explanation: Note: this hadith (Sunan Ibn Majah) is graded weak by some scholars. According to the Hadith, the Zakat (purifying charity) of the body is Roza (fasting). Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: During which times is fasting (Sawm) prohibited in Islam?

options.B: On the day of Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha

questions.explanation: Fasting (Sawm) is prohibited on the days of Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.

questions.text: Which days are referred to as the 'White Days' in Islam?
questions.explanation: The 'White Days' (Ayyam-e-Beed) in Islam refer to the 13th, 14th, and 15th of every Islamic month. Source: pakjobmcqs.com, saum.
